blocks.text: By way of a corollary I should like to add a Muhammadan fable about the bat. We believe that God the Father created all things through the eternal Word, that is, through Jesus Christ, his Son, for so Scripture teaches us. Thus David, Psalm. XXXIII, 6: By the word of the Lord the heavens were made. And Ioh. I, 3: All things were made through him, and without him was not anything made that was made. And 1 Cor. VIII, 6: One Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him. And Col. I, 16: By him were all things created that are in the heavens and that are on earth, visible and invisible, etc. All things were created through him and in him. And Hebr. I, 2: He has spoken to us in the Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the world. Hence Ioh. V, 19: Whatever he (the Father) does, these things the Son also does likewise. So say the Prophets and Apostles. But the circumcised doctors deny that Christ created anything except the bat. On what argument, let them see to it. For in the Sura of the Qur'an entitled ال عمران [Āl ʿImrān] The Family of Amran, whom they [col. 351] imagine to have been the father of Mary the virgin, Christ says that he creates birds: I have come to you, he says, with a sign from your Lord, اني اخلق لكم من الطين كهية الطير فانفخ فيها فيكون طيرا باذن الله [annī akhluqu lakum min al-ṭīn ka-hayʾat al-ṭayr fa-anfukhu fīhā fa-yakūnu ṭayran bi-idhn Allāh] I form for you out of clay something like the figure of a bird, and I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird, God so permitting. And in the Sura Almeida, that is, The Table, God addresses him thus: وان تخلق من الطين كهية الطير باذني فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا باذني [wa-idh takhluqu min al-ṭīn ka-hayʾat al-ṭayr bi-idhnī fa-tanfukhu fīhā fa-takūnu ṭayran bi-idhnī] And when you formed out of clay the image of a bird by my permission, and breathed into it, and by my leave it became a bird. But that these birds, forsooth, were bats, and that [III, 118] Jesus Christ created nothing besides, was divined by those who lived after Muhammad; because a bird of darkness seemed better suited to the temper of these men of darkness. Hence Alkazuinius: وانما طالب بنو اسرايل عيسي عليه السلام يخلق الخغاش لانه اتم الطير خلقه لان له اذنا واسنان وثديا فاتخذ من الطين [wa-innamā ṭālaba banū Isrāʾīl ʿĪsā ʿalayhi al-salām yakhluqu al-khughāsh li-annahu atammu al-ṭayr khalqahu li-anna lahu udhnan wa-asnān wa-thadyan fa-ittakhadha min al-ṭīn] Moreover the children of Israel asked Jesus, on whom be peace, to create a bat; because the bat is by its nature the most perfect, since it has ears, and teeth, and teats: and he took clay, etc. And Damir: الخغاش هو الذي خلقه عيسي بن مريم باذن الله [al-khughāsh huwa alladhī khalaqahu ʿĪsā ibn Maryam bi-idhn Allāh] The bat is the bird which Jesus, son of Mary, created by God's permission. And Ibno Abas: الطير الوطواط الذي نفخ فيها عيسي بن مريم وكان طيرا باذن الله عز وجل [al-ṭayr al-waṭwāṭ alladhī nafakha fīhā ʿĪsā ibn Maryam wa-kāna ṭayran bi-idhn Allāh ʿazza wa-jalla] The bird watwat (the bat), into which Jesus, son of Mary, breathed, and it became a bird, by permission of God, the mighty and glorious. And VVaheb, son of Manba: لما خلق عيسي عليه السلامّ الخغاش باذن الله كان يطير ما دام الناس ينظرون اليه فاذا غاب عن ابصارهم سقط ميتا الحكمة في ذلك ليبين فعل الخالق من فعل الخالق تعالي [lammā khalaqa ʿĪsā ʿalayhi al-salām al-khughāsh bi-idhn Allāh kāna yaṭīru mā dāma al-nās yanẓurūna ilayhi fa-idhā ghāba ʿan abṣārihim saqaṭa maytan al-ḥikma fī dhālika li-yubayyina fiʿl al-khāliq min fiʿl al-khāliq taʿālā] Why did Jesus, on whom be peace, by God's permission create a bat which does not cease flying while men look at it, but when they stop looking lies as if dead? So that we might know from this how much the work of a creature differs from the work of the Creator, who is the most high God. But, good sirs, if Christ created the bat only after he was born of the virgin, how did Moses, Isaiah, [col. 352] the Greek translators, Homer, Herodotus, Corinna, Plato, Aristotle, Clearchus, Antigonus, Nicander, Varro, and six hundred others mention it before Christ was born? Or, if Christ, son of Mary, created new individuals within a species that already existed and had been created by the most high God, then Christ's works differ in nothing from the works of that first Creator.
